Dated this the 13th day of September, 2024 This Criminal Miscellaneous Case has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, to qaush Annexure.A1 Final Report and all further proceedings in S.C. No.348/2019 on the files of the Special Court for the trial of cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act [hereinafter referred as 'POCSO Act' for short],
Muvattupuzha, arose out of Crime No.277/2019 of Piravom Police Station, Ernakulam.

sentences.text: The petitioner herein is the sole accused in the above case.
2. At the time of admission hearing, the learned counsel for the petitioner zealously argued, to quash the proceedings on the ground that the matter has been settled.

Since the offences alleged are punishable under Section 376(1) of IPC and under Section 3(a) read with 4 of the POCSO Act, on going through the records, this Court felt doubt regarding the stage of the case, even though it is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that 2024:KER:70016 trial not started in the case.
Hence, this Court called for a report from the learned Special Judge.

As per the report dated 12.09.2024, the learned Special Judge reported as under:
"I may humbly submit that the case is at the final hearing stage and evidence was already completed in this case.
It is seen from the records that earlier, prosecution evidence was completed in 2022 and questioning of the accused was also done on 09.05.2022.
Case was then heard U/s.232 Cr PC by my learned Predecessor and found to be not fit for acquittal there under.
Thereafter it was posted for defence evidence to 22.07.2022 and finally on 16.08.2022, defence evidence was closed and this case was posted for final arguments.
It is also seen that after several postings, on 21.09.2023, the Special Prosecutor had filed petition U/s.311 Cr PC as Crl MP No.963/2023.
That was allowed on 13.10.2023 and again PW15 was examined and Ext.P15 was marked on 26.10.2023.
Additional questioning of the accused was seen done on 30.11.2023.
Later, when 2024:KER:70016

the case was passed through the stage U/s.232 Cr PC and defence evidence and again posted for final arguments, it was reported by the Counsel before my learned predecessor that Crl MC 11312/2023 was filed before the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and thus my learned predecessor had adjourned the matter awaiting order from the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala."

3. Thus, it appears that, in this case, prosecution evidence completed and the case now stands posted for final hearing to deliver judgment and at this juncture, suppressing the said fact, this Crl.M.C. has been filed.
Noticing this, the learned counsel for the petitioner sought permission to withdraw this petition.

sentences.text: However, suppression of material facts is well discernible and this is not a fit case, wherein quashment of the proceedings can be resorted to on the basis of settlement, since offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Section 376(1) of IPC and under Section 3(a) read with 4 of the POCSO Act.

5. Hence, this petition stands dismissed, holding 2024:KER:70016 that the matter would require disposal on merits by the learned Special Judge, after hearing both sides, since evidence already completed.
6. Since, there is suppression of material facts, imposition of heavy cost is inevitable.

However, for the time being, the cost is limited to Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only) to be paid by the petitioner/accused before the District Legal Services Authority, Ernakulam, within a period of ten days from today and produce receipt before the Special Court, within seven days, thereafter.
On failure to effect payment as directed, the learned Special Judge is directed to proceed as per law to realize the amount as fine from the petitioner, without fail.
Registry shall forward a copy of this order to the Special Court forthwith for information and further action.
